newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut's latest CD issue oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut's latest CD issue oversubscribed.

text.p: Bank of Beirut said on Thursday its latest $5-million issue of fixed-rate dollar-denominated certificates of deposit launched this week was oversubscribed by $3.95 million.

The CDs, launched on Tuesday, bore the lowest interest rate of any of the 16 issues made by the bank since it began issuing floating-rate and fixed-rate certificates of deposit in foreign currencies in June 1995, the bank said in a statement.

"Bank of Beirut's last CD issue had a maturity of one-year, bore an interest rate of 7.5 percent per annum and had a total issue amount of $5 million. The amount actually subscribed to amounted to $8.95 million," it said.
"The bank was able to lower its interest rate on the CDs and still get an oversubscription due to the better positioning of the bank as at the end of 1996," it added.

Bank of Beirut said it ranked 15th among Lebanon's 82 banks in size of assets and loans and 16th in terms of customer deposits in 1996. It plans to list 30 percent of its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange shortly.
